rationales.LC: The attacker's natural-language chat message reaches the LegacyBot handler, which matches a regex and dumps credentials and PII from its prompt without any mediation.
rationales.CP: The finding is a single chat request against a stateless scripted handler; LegacyBot answers only the latest user message and stores nothing.
rationales.AP: The effect is confined to the LegacyBot reply; no handoff to another agent, tool, or principal occurs on this path.
rationales.RH: The path is a deterministic scripted reply with no evaluator, verifier, grader, or reward channel in the agent's reach; nothing on this path can be gamed.
rationales.ES: No tool, MCP server, or plugin is invoked; the sink is the scripted chat reply and the tool names in the persona are declared only.

rh_facts.locus: Scripted LegacyBot chat handler on port 7003; no evaluator, verifier, or reward channel exists on the path

score.automatable_rationale: The entire attack is a single unauthenticated HTTP chat request to a listening port whose reply contains the secrets; no human interaction with the target is required, so it can be scripted and run at machine speed.
score.technical_impact_rationale: The reply discloses the complete credential and PII set held in the agent's context (admin credentials, two API keys, database credentials, and user PII records), fully exposing the confidentiality scope of that component.

applicability_as_implemented.rationale: In the default simulated mode LegacyBot is a deterministic regex handler returning scripted text; no model call and no tool selection or sequencing occurs, only a fixed reply.

applicability_as_modeled.rationale: The lab models LegacyBot as a persona agent that declares tools (read_file, write_file, execute_command, send_email, access_database) and complies with attacker requests, i.e., an LLM-driven agent that selects among tools and pursues goals from natural language.
